issue.title: Fix fence on non-x86 arch and miri
issue.body:
The problem seems to be that the original author of this code confused fence in the x86 hardware memory model with atomic fence in the C++ memory model. (On x86, `lock cmpxchg; mov (load from memory)` is fine. See also https://www.cl.cam.ac.uk/~pes20/cpp/cpp0xmappings.html. On C++ memory model and many architectures, fence for load should be `load; fence`)

Fixes https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/issues/5164
FYI @cbeuw

body:
The fact that they advise to disable Stacked Borrows does not inspire a ton of confidence though. ;)

FWIW, latest Miri has `-Zmiri-track-weak-memory-loads`, which should help diagnose this issue. But OTOH @cbeuw [pretty much figured it out already](https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/pull/4988#issuecomment-1167973221) I think; someone probably needs to go fix smol-rs/concurrent-queue.
Ah looks like this is tracked in concurrent-queue: https://github.com/smol-rs/concurrent-queue/issues/17

The problem in concurrent-queue that we agreed on is that it was using x86-specific fences that Miri does not understand. This has been fixed in concurrent-queue 1.2.4 (https://github.com/smol-rs/concurrent-queue/commit/d61005fc792bcd9a20ae9f61726b6842211cc10a).

> that Miri does not understand

To be more precise, using those fences is just wrong when writing Rust code, and Miri understands and detects that correctly. They can only be used correctly when writing inline assembly.
